actions: Re-attempted exact Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.16441066 artifact discovery using public web transport only. The peer-reviewed article still identifies this DOI as the official code artifact, but the available transport did not expose the record file list/checksums in this invocation.
Searched exact-title, DOI, and distinctive-phrase variants for a non-author PRG rerun or failure report. No clear independent exact rerun was found.

Repeated the prior attractor-necessity intervention across three independently trained source-derived recurrent base models. Unlike the previous reduced T=40 test, all three models were trained on T=100 moving-input sequences with tau=2, per-step layer normalization, all-time direction supervision, 12 directions, and p=0.01 binary noise. Hidden size and image generator remained reduced/source-derived rather than exact paper settings.

For each base model, decoded a 2D direction subspace from late hidden activity using cos(theta),sin(theta); baseline circular-distance Spearman values were 0.868, 0.759, and 0.861 on the matched calibration sets.

Applied tangent-selective recurrent 2D perturbations and equal-rank residual-subspace controls. Instead of label-only readout refitting, fitted the perturbed linear readouts directly to the clean base-model logits by ridge regression, and separately selected perturbation magnitudes so tangent and residual controls matched clean-logit RMSE closely. Mean absolute calibration-RMSE mismatch across 12 matched perturbation pairs was 0.00762.

Across four perturbation draws per base, mean tangent-minus-residual all-gap interpolation deltas were +0.50 percentage points for base 1, -0.25 points for base 2, and -0.45 points for base 3. Overall mean was -0.067 points; a hierarchical bootstrap over bases and perturbation draws gave a 95% interval of approximately [-1.12,+0.93] points. The previous small negative interpolation effect therefore did not replicate across independently trained bases.

Matched clean-accuracy deltas were small overall (+0.18 points tangent minus residual). Direction-subspace smoothness changed negligibly relative to residual controls (mean Spearman difference +0.00042), and a source-derived post-switch flow-alignment surrogate likewise showed no consistent tangent-specific change (mean difference -0.00448; base-level signs were mixed).

Broadened public-source scanning after the causal downgrade and identified intrinsic Top-Down Stabilization (iTDS; Nature Communications 2026) as a new high-priority quantitative neuroscience-to-AI lead. iTDS adds an output-derived slow top-down signal to supervised plasticity; the article reports evaluation across 16 tasks and architectures, 91/100 independently initialized chaotic-RNN simulations outperforming the sigma=0 baseline, ten-fold-cross-validated MNIST generalization gains at moderate stabilization, and increased perturbation tolerance averaged over 500 test patterns. Public code is deposited at Figshare DOI 10.6084/m9.figshare.31146457 and includes reservoir, BPTT, CIFAR-10/100, Fashion-MNIST, SVHN, and ResNet50 examples. Exact benchmark deltas from the deposited code/source-data were not extracted in this invocation, so promotion remains provisional.

public_sources.title: Representation Transfer via Invariant Input-driven Continuous Attractors for Fast Domain Adaptation
facts_used: Peer-reviewed PRG uses 512-neuron vanilla RNN modules, tau=2, per-step layer normalization, all-time cross-entropy, synthetic motion primitives and reports low-dimensional input-driven manifolds with recovery from off-manifold perturbations.

public_sources.title: Intrinsic stabilization of synaptic plasticity improves learning and robustness in artificial neural networks
facts_used: iTDS combines supervised error with an output-derived top-down error whose target is a slow filtered copy of network output.
Evaluated across 16 synthetic and real tasks in reservoir, recurrent/BPTT and feedforward networks.
In a chaotic-RNN experiment, 91 of 100 independent initializations with iTDS outperformed sigma=0.
MNIST evaluation uses 10-fold cross-validation and 500 recurrent units; moderate stabilization improves learning/generalization while excessive stabilization can hurt generalization.
Noise-robustness analysis averages the number of perturbation iterations to misclassification over 500 test patterns.

public_sources.title: Code accompanying Intrinsic Stabilization of Synaptic Plasticity Improves Learning and Robustness in Artificial Neural Networks
facts_used: Includes reservoir1.m, reservoir_chaos1.m, reservoir_class1.m, BPTT1.m and Python CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100/ResNet50/SVHN/Fashion-MNIST examples.
Repository notes that only partial/simple tasks are provided and outputs include classification error/loss.

intervention.control: rank-matched perturbation in random residual 2D subspace
intervention.clean_matching: distill perturbed readout to clean base logits by ridge regression; choose target/control perturbation magnitudes independently from a small grid to match clean-logit RMSE

multi_base_necessity_test.interpretation: The previous single-base necessity signal does not replicate across independently trained T=100 base models when tangent and residual perturbations are matched more tightly by clean-logit functional effect. This downgrades attractor-specific causal evidence. Primitive isolation and all-time temporal supervision remain the better-supported mechanisms from this branch. The negative result is limited to this reduced generator, hidden size, trained bases, perturbation family, interpolation corruption and functional-matching procedure; it does not refute the paper's full 512-unit PRG or input-driven continuous attractors generally.

evidence_added_this_run: Three-base T=100 replication of the reduced necessity intervention did not reproduce a consistent tangent-subspace-specific interpolation penalty.
Clean-logit functional matching reduced target/control mismatch but yielded mixed base-level robustness signs and an interval spanning zero.
Direction smoothness and the local flow-alignment surrogate did not show consistent tangent-specific degradation.
candidate_update.interpretation: Retain PRG as a strong empirical transfer architecture, but further reduce confidence that low-dimensional attractor geometry itself is the dominant causal source of robustness. Primitive disentanglement, synthetic pretraining and distributed temporal supervision remain the leading supported transferable ingredients.

new_candidate.mechanism: A slow output-derived top-down trace is compared with current network output and its error term is combined with supervised plasticity, dynamically damping unstable synaptic updates while gradient-alignment is strongest early in learning.
quantitative_evidence: 91/100 independently initialized chaotic-RNN runs with iTDS outperform the sigma=0 baseline in the paper's matched-initialization comparison.
MNIST uses 10-fold cross-validation with 500 recurrent units and reports improved learning/generalization for moderate iTDS, but exact plotted accuracy deltas were not recovered this run.
Noise-robustness assays average perturbation-to-misclassification over 500 test patterns and report higher tolerance with iTDS.
Paper evaluates 16 tasks across reservoir, recurrent/BPTT and feedforward architectures.
scope: The core rule still depends on an externally supervised target; this is stabilization of supervised plasticity, not unsupervised biological credit assignment.
Moderate sigma is beneficial but excessive stabilization can worsen generalization or cause instability.
Exact CIFAR/Fashion/SVHN deltas and independent replication were not established in this run.
Public Figshare provides code examples, but it explicitly says only partial/simple tasks are provided; deposited outputs/source data still need audit.

exact_next_action: Shift the primary causal branch away from PRG attractor necessity unless exact artifact recovery or an independent rerun appears. Next audit the iTDS Figshare package at DOI 10.6084/m9.figshare.31146457: recover file-level code where possible, extract exact CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100/Fashion-MNIST/SVHN and MNIST effect sizes, identify whether comparisons are seed-matched and whether top-down stabilization is equivalent to a simpler output-EMA/gradient-rescaling regularizer. Run a minimal source-matched control that compares iTDS against supervised learning plus an explicit generic gradient-damping/output-consistency baseline. Continue public search for independent iTDS reproduction/failure reports and exact PRG reruns. Keep PRG evidence scope narrowed unless stronger source-matched causality emerges.
